Shah Md. Munir Sharif with Mohammad Imran Jahangir, Advocates-For the Petitioner. 
Masud Ahmed Sayeed, Advocate-For Respondent No.2-Bank.
parties:
Sheuly Khanam ----- Petitioner
Vs
Artha Rin Adalat 2nd Court, Dhaka and others ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
Md. Ashfaqul Islam J: This Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the Order of issuance of certificate under Section 33(5) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 vide Order No. 24 dated 24-06-2007 (Annexure-D) so far it relates to the property of the petitioner issued by respondent No. 1 in Artha Rin Execution Case No. 252 of 2005 shall not be declared to have been issued without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 2. The background leading to the Rule, in short, is that respondent No. 2-Janata Bank. Limited, Ramna Corporate Branch, Dhaka as plaintiff instituted a Suit before the Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, 1st Court, Dhaka for recovery of outstanding dues against the petitioner and others (defendants) by enforcing mortgage and the same was registered as Title Suit No. 384 of 2003. Subsequently the same was renumbered as Artha Rin Suit No.12 of 2005. The suit was decreed ex-parte and subsequently the same was put in to execution by Execution Case No. 252 of 20.05 by the respondent Bank. Thereafter in compliance with section 33(1) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 the decree holder Bank went for auction of the mortgaged property. On 05-03-2007 three bidders participated in auction and the Adalat cancelled the bid holding that the value of the property is more than the bid amount. Subsequent to that respondent No. 2 Bank on 8-4-2007 filed an application before the Adalat and prayed for issuing certificate under section 33(5) which was allowed by the Adalat on 24-06-2007 vide order No. 24 (Annexure-D) and the Execution Case was disposed of in terms of section 33(9) of the Ain. Against the said order the petitioner moved this Division and obtained the present Rule and stay. 

 3. Mr. Shah Md. Munir Sharif, the learned counsel for the petitioner after placing the petition, impugned order and other relevant. Annexures mainly submits that the provision of Section 33(5) of the Ain, 2003 clearly stipulates that if the property could not be sold in auction according to the provisions as laid down in sub-section (i)(ii)(iii) and (iv), the property in question shall be vested in the possession of decree-holder till the realization of decreed money and the decree-holder shall sell the decreed property according to the provisions of sub-section (i)(ii) and (iv) for unrealized decreetal amount and the Court shall issue a certificate. The respondent No. 1 issued certificate under Section 33(5) without following the provisions of Section 33(1) of Ain, 2003 and therefore, the certificate was issued violating the provisions of section 33(5) of Ain, 2003 as such the impugned order is without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. He further submits that in the instant case certificate was issued including the property of third party mortgagor along with the property of principal borrower violating the provision of sub-section 5 of section 6 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and for that reason the certificate itself is illegal and any auction pursuant to such certificate is without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 4. Mr. Masud Ahmed Sayeed, the learned counsel for the respondent bank on the other hand, by filing affidavit-in-opposition submits that the issuing of certificate by the respondent No. 1 under section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 in Artha Rin Execution Case No. 252 of 2005 is fully in accordance with law and hence this writ petition filed by the petitioner should be discharged outright. According to the certificate issued under section 33(5) of the Ain it appears that the respondent has been given ownership of the scheduled 'Ka', 'Kha' and 'Ga' properties and according to the Title Deeds which are submitted with the respondent it appears that the owner of schedule (Ka) property is Sheikh Mahtabuddin, the owner of Schedule (Kha) property is the present petitioner Sheuly Khanam and the owner of the schedule (Ga) property is Kazi Mahbubur Rahman. The petitioner is not a Director nor shareholder of respondent No. 3 company. The respondent No. 3 enjoyed credit facilities from the respondent No.2. The petitioner is the owner of the Schedule 'Ga' property included in the certificate. In the plaint of Artha Rin Suit No. 12 of 2005 described the status of the petitioner as mortgagor and the respondent No.4 and 6 are of the owner of schedule- Ka and Kha property included in the certificate under section 33(5). 

 5. Heard the learned counsel of both sides and considered their submissions at length. On several occasions we have given our patient hearing of the case on this issue. 

 6. The moot question that faces this Division in this writ petition is whether under the facts and circumstances of the case issuing certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain so far as it relates to the petitioner should be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 7. We have found that upon a meticulous adherence to terms of section 33 respondent-banks went for auction of the mortgaged property but cancelled the auction sale since the price was shockingly low. At that point of time as per section 33(5) of the Ain on the prayer of respondent bank the Adalat issued certificate in favour of the bank and execution proceeding thereby disposed of in terms of section 33(9). We do not find any illegality in the process of issuing certificate in the instant case. 

 8. At the outset we would like to record our observation that the petitioner as it could be found in Annexure-'D' the order sheets of the Money Execution Case No. 252 of 2005 that in order No. 11 dated 05-03-2007 it has been clearly mentioned by the executing Court that:— 

 "Mr. AJ Mohammad Ali, the learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that the certificate issued under section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 in favour of the decree-holder bank is only for possession and enjoyment of the mortgaged property and it did not mean final disposal of the Execution case for which further action for disposal of the suit property is necessary under section 33(7) of the said Act, but the High Court Division misconstrued the provision of section 33(9) in holding that the Execution case was finally disposed of and thereby erred in summarily rejecting the writ petition. He lastly submits that the decree being in preliminary form, the suit remained pending and thus the Artha Rin Adalat had the jurisdiction to consider the application for stay under section 44 of the Act and to grant installment payment under section 49 of the Act, but the Artha Rin Adalat failed to exercise its jurisdiction on the erroneous view of law that it became functus officio and had no jurisdiction to decide the application on merit.
